faq.answer: No. Facilitation, sales work, community organizing, caregiving logistics, and short deadlines may require those strategies. Recheck the pattern after coordination duties and time pressure change instead of typing from one task.
faq.question: Do multiple options, social coordination, and active experiments prove 6w7?

faq.answer: Hold the information gap and deadline steady while removing any duty to coordinate a group. Compare 6w7 option generation and ally contact with 6w5 source validation and quiet analysis, then record whether the voluntary strategy changes.
faq.question: How should 6w7 be compared with 6w5?

faq.answer: Comfortably using one supported route, sustaining solitary review, and declining unnecessary coordination, followed by stopping at a reasonable threshold, should lower confidence in the 6w7 modifier.
faq.question: What evidence weakens the 6w7 modifier?

sections.body_md: Confirm that repeated contingency planning and trust checking support a Type Six account before interpreting the person's option generation or ally contact. Consider those coordination patterns only as a secondary 6w7 modifier after facilitation, sales work, community organizing, caregiving logistics, and short deadlines no longer explain the behavior.
sections.title: Keep Type Six primary before adding a modifier

sections.body_md: Give 6w7 and 6w5 the same incomplete task with matched consequence, deadline, and decision rights. Compare how option generation, ally contact, and reversible experiments differ from 6w5 source validation and quiet analysis in moving the work forward.
sections.title: Compare 6w7 with 6w5 on one uncertain task

sections.body_md: Across an incident response, social plan, and individual choice, record requested information, consulted people, option narrowing, action time, and stopping rule. Distinguish coordination chosen under uncertainty from coordination required by the role.
sections.title: Observe choices, handoffs, and stopping rules

sections.body_md: Reduce confidence when the person comfortably uses one supported route, sustains solitary review, or declines unnecessary coordination. Treat those choices as counterexamples rather than exceptions to 6w7.
sections.title: Use flexible low-stakes action as a challenge

sections.body_md: Facilitation, sales work, community organizing, caregiving logistics, and short deadlines can all require rapid option generation and ally contact. Audit these demands before retaining a 6w7 explanation.
sections.title: Audit learned work and environmental demands

sections.body_md: Treat 6w7 only as an evidence-limited comparison beside the Type Six core. It neither measures extraversion or optimism nor forecasts social ability, loyalty, or conduct.
sections.title: Keep the modifier secondary and evidence-limited

sections.body_md:
Duration: 5

Context: Across five days, observe one incident response, one collaborative plan, and one individual decision where several routes are available.

Observable signal: Record who is contacted, options proposed, route selected, experiment size, deadline, decision owner, and what evidence closes the option search.

Page-specific signal: Compare whether coordination produces a decision update or merely keeps more possibilities active after one reversible route is ready.

Alternative explanation: Check facilitation duty, sales work, community organizing, caregiving logistics, emergency response, and time pressure.

Reflection prompt: Find one event where a single written route or solitary review was sufficient, and use it to lower confidence in the 6w7 modifier.

seo.description: 6w7 is an evidence-limited wing hypothesis: Type Six uncertainty, support, trust, and contingency concerns remain primary, while the adjacent type may modify attention toward options, social coordination, and active experiments. The pattern does not establish 6w7 because facilitation duties, incident response, sales work, community organizing, and time pressure can require the same behavior.
seo.title: 6w7: a core-first hypothesis about options, social coordination, and active experiments
